name: Photographer's Assistant
seoTitle: Business Insurance Cost for Photographer's Assistants
seoDescription: Calculate estimated business insurance costs for photographer's assistant businesses including general liability and professional E&O coverage.

industryContext.contextNote: Photographer's assistants support shoots by handling equipment and logistics rather than owning client relationships directly, giving them a narrower liability profile than lead photographers.

riskFactors.title: Equipment Handling Damage
riskFactors.description: Assistants regularly carry and set up cameras, lighting, and grip equipment, creating risk of accidental damage to gear they don't own.

riskFactors.title: On-Set Property Damage
riskFactors.description: Moving lighting stands, backdrops, or props on location can accidentally damage a client's or venue's property.

riskFactors.title: On-Set Injury
riskFactors.description: Handling heavy equipment and cables on a busy shoot set creates trip-and-fall and lifting-injury risk.

faqs.question: Why do photographer's assistants need General Liability insurance?
faqs.answer: Many production companies and venues require anyone working on-set, including assistants, to carry proof of General Liability before allowing access.

faqs.question: What is the average cost of business insurance for a photographer's assistant?
faqs.answer: A photographer's assistant in the $0-50k revenue tier pays an estimated $250 per year for baseline General Liability coverage, one of the lowest tiers in this calculator.

faqs.question: Does an assistant need their own coverage if the lead photographer has insurance?
faqs.answer: The lead photographer's policy typically doesn't extend to independent assistants, so most assistants carry their own General Liability coverage.

faqs.question: Do assistants need an equipment floater if they don't own the gear?
faqs.answer: Assistants generally don't need an equipment floater for gear they don't own, though they should confirm liability if they're responsible for equipment damage while handling it.

blogContent.whyThisRiskFactor: Photographer's assistants carry a 0.85 actuarial risk factor, reflecting lower exposure than lead photographers since they don't typically own the equipment or client contract.
blogContent.howCalculated: Premiums scale with revenue tier and General Liability coverage sized to on-set access requirements.
blogContent.comparisonNote: Photographer's assistant premiums are among the lowest creative-services tiers, below lead freelance photographers and videographers.
